disclaimer: These are general, nonclinical planning notes written for PawPal+. They are illustrative defaults for scheduling purposes only and are not veterinary advice; always defer to a licensed veterinarian for an individual animal's needs.

snippets.text: Adult dogs generally do well with at least 30 minutes of walking activity a day, often split across one or two walks depending on breed energy level and age.
snippets.source: PawPal+ Care Guide: Canine Exercise Basics

snippets.text: Adult dogs are commonly fed once or twice daily; the feeding session itself (serving, supervising, cleanup) typically takes about 10 minutes.
snippets.source: PawPal+ Care Guide: Canine Feeding Basics

snippets.text: Administering routine medication to a dog is usually brief, around 5 minutes, but consistency of timing matters more than the exact duration.
Short haired dogs typically need brushing sessions of 10 to 15 minutes a few times a week; long haired breeds often need 20 to 30 minutes to prevent matting.
Puzzle toys, short training games, or play sessions of about 15 to 20 minutes help prevent boredom related behavior issues in dogs.
Cats rarely need a formal walk; instead, 10 to 15 minutes of structured interactive play (wand toys, chasing) is commonly used to meet activity needs.
snippets.source: PawPal+ Care Guide: Feline Activity Basics

snippets.text: Cats are often fed in smaller, more frequent meals; each individual feeding session typically takes about 5 to 10 minutes.
snippets.source: PawPal+ Care Guide: Feline Feeding Basics

snippets.text: Giving medication to a cat (including pilling) can take 5 to 10 minutes once time to calm the animal is included.
Short haired cats mostly self groom but benefit from 5 to 10 minutes of brushing weekly; long haired cats often need 15 to 20 minutes several times a week.
Interactive toys or short clicker training sessions of 10 to 15 minutes help satisfy a cat's natural hunting instincts and reduce boredom.
Small mammals and other pets that are not dogs or cats often benefit from short, supervised time outside their enclosure (about 15 minutes) rather than a formal walk.
snippets.source: PawPal+ Care Guide: General Activity Basics

snippets.text: Feeding routines for small or exotic pets are usually quick, typically around 5 to 10 minutes depending on species.
snippets.source: PawPal+ Care Guide: General Feeding Basics

snippets.text: Medication for small or exotic pets should be given at a consistent time each day; the session itself is typically brief, around 5 minutes.
Grooming needs vary widely across small and exotic pets; a general check and clean session of 10 to 15 minutes is a reasonable planning default.
Novel objects, foraging opportunities, or supervised exploration time of 15 to 20 minutes supports mental stimulation for small and exotic pets.
Recurring medication tasks are generally scheduled at the same time each day; a consistent routine reduces the chance of a missed or doubled dose.
